//cli-gate: The `src/cli/**` exclusion above is NOT the whole story since 2026-07-28. Three CLI files are the highest-consequence code in the package: cli/studio.ts has a WRITE MODE that executes mutations and a PII redaction path, cli/migrate.ts runs destructive DDL, and cli/destructive.ts is the scanner that decides what counts as destructive. They were unmeasured, which hid the fact that they are ALREADY well tested (studio-write.test.ts is 1,546 lines, studio-demo.test.ts 973, migrate.test.ts 771) and, worse, left no ratchet on them: coverage could fall to zero without any gate noticing. They now have their OWN gate, `npm run test:coverage:cli`, run as its own CI job. It is a SEPARATE c8 invocation rather than an entry in the `include` list here because c8 checks one threshold set per run: folding these files into this run would let a studio.ts regression hide behind the query runtime's numbers, which is the same masking the blanket exclusion produced. SUPERSEDED 2026-08-23, on the part about cli/index.ts. That sentence read: 'cli/index.ts stays out of both gates: it is 4,759 lines of argument parsing and command dispatch whose behavior is asserted through the CLI end-to-end tests, and its uncovered `process.exit` paths would dominate any floor set over it.' Every clause of it is still true and the conclusion did not follow. The file is now 5,945 lines, the largest in the repo, and 'a floor over it would be dominated by process.exit paths' is an argument for a LOW floor, not for no floor: the point of the ratchet is that the number cannot fall silently, which is the same argument this note already makes two sentences earlier for the other CLI files. It is in `coverage:cli:collect` and holds `coverage:cli:gate:index` at 30/30/73/18 against a measured 32.62/32.62/75.62/20. It is deliberately NOT in the aggregate, because at 5,945 lines and 33% it would drag that gate from 89.63 to 66.32 lines and force two floors down by about 25 points; see //coverage:cli:gate:aggregate in package.json. `scripts/check-coverage-gate-sync.mjs` is what keeps a collected file from ending up held by neither.
//cli-gate-per-file: The CLI gate is PER FILE, not aggregate-only, since 2026-07-28. An aggregate floor lets the least-covered file spend the slack the best-covered file earned, which is the same masking the blanket `src/cli/**` exclusion produced, one level down: measured on 0.61.0 the three files hold 2960/3662 lines (80.83%), an 80% floor needs 2930, so there were 30 covered lines of slack, ALL of which migrate.ts could spend by falling from 70.27% to 68.18% with the aggregate still green. c8 cannot express three different floors in one invocation (`--per-file` applies the SAME numbers to every file), so `npm run test:coverage:cli` is now one collection run plus four `c8 report --check-coverage` passes over the coverage already on disk, three per-file and one aggregate. Re-reporting costs no extra test run. The aggregate pass is KEPT, it is the only thing that catches all three files sagging together inside their individual margins. A gate run with no collected coverage exits 1 (ENOENT on coverage/tmp) rather than reporting a vacuous pass, which is checked.

//merge-bug: WHY THE REPORT IS NOT `c8 report`. c8 merges every process's V8 coverage into one ProcessCov (mergeProcessCovs, @bcoe/v8-coverage) BEFORE converting anything to istanbul, and that merge is NOT MONOTONIC: adding a process's coverage can lower the merged result. Measured 2026-08-16 on this suite's own 359 process files, query/relations.ts covered lines by number of files merged: 10->1565, 40->2216, 80->2495, 160->2918, 240->3043, then 359->1333. The collapse is a cliff, not a slope, and bisects to a single added file. Mechanism, visible in the raw JSON: V8 compiles functions lazily, so a process that merely imports a module reports a different function set for it (110 functions in one process, 86 in another, same source file), and merging range trees that disagree about the function set loses counts. c8's own source carries a TODO about the merge implementation. THE PROOF that the number was not coverage: a 448-test SUBSET of this suite reported relations.ts at 91.88% while the full 5,819-test superset reported 41.78%. A superset cannot cover less than its subset. THE FIX is a reorder, not a reimplementation: scripts/coverage-report.mjs feeds the per-process ScriptCovs to the conversion loop unmerged, so the combining is done by istanbul-lib-coverage's merge, which is additive and monotonic by construction. Everything else stays c8's, including this file, the reporters, and the checkCoverages gate. VALIDATION: the fixed merge agrees with stock c8 EXACTLY wherever stock c8 was still monotonic (10 files 1565, 80 files 2495, 240 files 3043) and diverges only past the collapse; it is monotonic across the same series; and src/connection-url.ts, independently measured at 100% in isolation, reads 100% under it and 40% under stock c8. CHECKED AND UNAFFECTED: the src/cli/** gate (see //cli-gate) collects only ~24 process files, below the collapse, and re-reporting it under the fixed merge moves lines and functions by ZERO and branches by +0.5, so its floors were honest and it stays on stock c8. Revisit that if its file list grows a lot.
